question.text: Shares with Differential Voting Rights (DVR) allow promoters to:

answer.text: Raise risk capital without diluting their ownership stake and control, while offering investors higher dividends with lower voting rights
Raise debt capital while maintaining equity-like features
Issue shares only to foreign institutional investors
Avoid listing the company on any stock exchange

explanation.text: The Logic: DVR shares allow promoters to raise risk capital without diluting their ownership stake and control. Investors in DVR shares generally enjoy a higher rate of dividend but have proportionately lower voting rights compared to investors in ordinary equity shares. The Trap: DVR shares are equity instruments, not debt (option B). They can be issued to any investor, not just FIIs (option C). Companies issuing DVR shares can still be listed (option D).
